lines.t: Your Gatorade got smaller. Same price. And you probably didn't notice.
lines.title: IT *SHRANK*

lines.t: Gatorade swapped its thirty-two ounce bottle for twenty-eight ounces. That's twelve and a half percent less drink.
lines.title: LESS *DRINK*
lines.label: less per bottle

lines.t: Which means you pay about fourteen percent more per ounce. Without the price tag changing at all.
lines.label: More per ounce
lines.title: HIDDEN *PRICE HIKE*

lines.t: It's called shrinkflation. Toblerone did it too. In twenty sixteen, the UK four-hundred-gram bar became three hundred sixty… by making bigger gaps between the triangles.
lines.title: TOBLERONE *UK 2016*

lines.t: Why do companies do it? Because we notice a higher price. But we almost never check the weight.
lines.title: DO YOU *CHECK?*

lines.t: The fix: look at the unit price on the shelf tag. Price per ounce never lies.
lines.title: THE *FIX*

lines.t: What shrank on you? Tell me in the comments. Follow for more.
lines.title: WHAT *SHRANK?*
